findings.reason: §8 must either extend `resolve_service_url` to own the remote auto-tunnel (env override, `ensure_tunnel`, `TUNNEL_OFFSET`) or state that `profiles.py` retains its remote-tunnel branch, otherwise "one owner" is not behaviour-preserving.
findings.text: §8 says `profiles.py` will "call `resolve_service_url`" and "carry no squeue call or loopback rewrite of their own", but the graph client's remote branch does work the owner does not: the `IMAS_CODEX_TUNNEL_BOLT_<HOST>` override, `ensure_tunnel(...)` with `TUNNEL_OFFSET`, and the tunnel-port URL (`bolt://localhost:{bolt_port+offset}`), whereas `resolve_service_url` (`remote/locations.py:282-283`) returns only `{protocol}://localhost:{port}` with no tunnel establishment or offset — so a worker following §8 literally drops remote Neo4j auto-tunnelling and breaks off-cluster graph access

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `resolve_remote_environment` (`remote/environment.py`) hides the block-vs-data-system-vs-caller precedence behind one function, and §8 collapses four SLURM-discovery copies onto one `resolve_service_url` interface rather than adding modules.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names owners rather than forking: §8 identifies the four existing SLURM-discovery copies (`remote/locations.py`, `settings.py`, `embeddings/readiness.py`, `graph/profiles.py`) and §6 retires `data_access_patterns.setup_commands`, whose existence before commit `8f50f6642` is confirmed by that commit's own diff.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every interface-touching section accounts in its own text (§2 retires the prototype's `class:`/`shots:`/`udpid:` keyword parking, §3 states why no existing WikiPage property can be retired, §6 retires `data_access_patterns.setup_commands` and states its scan-gate refusal reuses `missing_required`/`version_too_old` rather than adding a family, §8 adds none and removes two private copies).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's prior-art claims hold for §2/§3/§4/§6/§7 (verified against `schemas/facility.yaml`, `discovery/wiki/pipeline.py`, `discovery/signals/parallel.py`, `remote/environment.py`), but §8's unification onto `resolve_service_url` is incomplete: the owner does not carry the graph client's remote auto-tunnel behaviour.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section adds a wrapper over existing machinery without justification: §6 keeps the executor facility-agnostic and states why the resolver sits in the facility-aware layer, §8 adds no public definition, §3 reuses the existing edge writer rather than forking it.
